study_label: Etanercept versus saline placebo in recent acute myocardial infarction

objective.value: To study the effects of the TNF-α receptor antagonist etanercept on peripheral vasomotor and fibrinolytic function and platelet activation in patients presenting with recent acute myocardial infarction.

population.value: Patients with recent acute myocardial infarction at a tertiary referral cardiac centre: myocardial ischaemia lasting >20 minutes within 24 hours of hospitalisation, ischaemic ECG changes, and troponin-I >0.2 µg/l. Key exclusions included significant comorbidity, active systemic inflammatory disorders, insulin-dependent diabetes, anti-inflammatory drugs other than aspirin, and recent/recurrent infection, tuberculosis, or opportunistic infection within the prior 6 months.

duration_follow_up.value: Participants were evaluated before treatment and 24 hours after intravenous etanercept or saline placebo.

effect_result.value: PMA and platelet P-selectin expression were similar between groups at baseline. Following etanercept, PMA increased by 50% relative to baseline (30±5% vs 20±3%; p=0.02), whereas PMA was unaffected following saline placebo (28±5% vs 33±6%; p=0.23).

safety.value: No serious adverse events occurred during the study.

sample_size.randomized: 26 patients enrolled; the extracted evidence does not explicitly confirm that all 26 were randomized.
sample_size.analyzed: 15 underwent vascular assessment (8 randomized to etanercept).
sample_size.planned: At least 12 paired samples were estimated to provide 80% power.
sample_size.display: 26 enrolled; 15 underwent vascular assessment (8 etanercept); planned ≥12 paired samples

evidence_questions.objective: To assess the effects of etanercept on platelet activation, including the primary outcome of platelet-monocyte aggregate, in recent acute myocardial infarction.
evidence_questions.population: Patients with recent acute myocardial infarction meeting clinical, ECG, and troponin-I inclusion criteria.
